_comment: PROVISIONAL. NORTHERN OLD WORLD tile carved from the Games Workshop 'Warhammer: The Old World' interactive map (start_warhammer_old_world_z10.png, the stitched z10 relief tiles), placed by the paired-anchor-dot workflow validated on the Empire (2026-08-14). The user cropped the northern Old World out of the parent tile map and drew matched colour dots on the crop AND on terraqueous_globe_reprojected.png, which IS the canvas/mask frame (8192x3616). The dots use a 5-LEVEL-per-channel marker palette (each channel in {0,63,127,191,255}); each is a single compact 4x4 (12 px) blob. Recovering ALL non-grayscale ink in the grayscale crop finds 42 dots; 39 pair to a single clean canonical dot on the globe directly, and 2 more (maroon 127,0,0 and dark-maroon 63,0,0, which collide with the globe's natural dark-red speckle) are recovered by predicting their globe position through the fit and finding the lone canonical dot within ~15 px of the prediction. The user then flagged the top-edge dot c_3f00ff (63,0,255) as an incorrect pick and it was removed, leaving 40 pairs. objective=landmarks means NO silhouette fit (the drift-prone stage), just thin-plate interpolation. master_shape is the crop's native (h,w)=(4958,6134); the source will be the dot-free crop. This record only PLACES the tile; no geometry is extracted yet. Exclusion of the out-of-scope area is done by the CROP itself (the user cropped the parent down to the northern Old World rectangle) rather than by an alpha mask, so the whole opaque frame is intentionally in-scope and 'warp alpha>0 only' warps the full rectangle by design. ONE dot dropped as globe-side unrecoverable: muddy-teal (63,127,127) — no canonical dot found near its predicted globe position (the user did not place it on the globe). The two dark-red dots that first looked unrecoverable (maroon and dark-maroon) were recovered by the fit-predicted windowed search described above. NOTE: unlike the tww3 parchment tiles this is a grayscale RELIEF map, not a drawn-boundary network, so its downstream consumption is undecided (placement-only for now).
_comment_lattice: 16x16 over the crop (~380 master px horizontal spacing, ~310 vertical). With 39 landmarks a coarse 6x6=36-point lattice UNDER-samples the landmark field and smooths it away (measured: the resampled warp drifted up to 33 px from the dots; 12x12 cut that to 11); 16x16=256 points sample the 39-landmark thin-plate densely enough that the committed control_points reproduce every dot to mean 2 / max 5 px (the 5 px is the lone top-edge dot in the steep-gradient zone; the rest sub-pixel). The 39 dots blanket the crop interior AND its coastal/edge extremes; the lattice carries the affine trend into the crop corners, where it extrapolates beyond the dot hull. The far-south dots carry the largest non-affine curvature, which the thin-plate absorbs exactly at each dot. NOTE the northern Norsca coast is still dot-sparse: after c_3f00ff was removed the top edge is anchored only by c_3f00bf on the west shore, so the north coast is loose against the mask pending more northern dots.
_comment_landmarks: source px = dot centroid in the crop's own 6134x4958 frame (x,y); canvas px = the SAME dot's centroid read straight off terraqueous_globe_reprojected.png (= canvas space, no globe-fit indirection). Paired by exact 5-level palette colour; name is the dot's 6-digit hex (c_RRGGBB). Each is a single compact 4x4 component in both frames. 40 pairs (38 direct + 2 dark-red recovered via fit-predicted windowed search); muddy-teal (63,127,127) excluded as not-on-globe, and c_3f00ff removed as a user-flagged bad pick. These ARE the fit (not a held-out check) for objective=landmarks.

record.notes: PROVISIONAL — PLACEMENT ONLY, downstream consumption undecided. Northern Old World crop of the Games Workshop 'Warhammer: The Old World' interactive map (start_warhammer_old_world_z10.png, stitched z10 relief tiles), registered against tools/derived/land_sea_mask.png by tools/fit_registration.py --seed start_warhammer_old_world_northern (objective=landmarks; 40 user-drawn paired anchor dots, 5-level marker palette; 16x16 lattice; 38 read direct off terraqueous_globe_reprojected.png + 2 dark-red dots recovered by fit-predicted windowed search; muddy-teal 63,127,127 dropped as not-on-globe, and c_3f00ff removed as a user-flagged bad pick). Unlike the tww3 Old World mod parchment tiles this is a GRAYSCALE RELIEF tile with NO drawn boundary network, so it is NOT an ink_bridged boundary source; its role/precedence here are provisional lows pending the user's decision on how (or whether) it is consumed. Out-of-scope area is excluded by the crop itself (not by alpha), so the full opaque rectangle is in-scope by design. Contributes NO coastline (the mask remains the sole authority, user decision #1). PROVISIONAL until the user accepts the diagnostic render. MACHINE-FITTED; re-derive from the seed, do not hand-edit.
